book: The Conference of the Birds — Selections

1: The birds of the world gathered before the hoopoe, who wore the crest of a king and the wisdom of a traveller. He said: We have a king — the Simurgh — but no one has sought him. I know the road. Who will come? And the birds made excuses, each his own, and the hoopoe answered each one, for every excuse is a chain, and every chain has a key.

The nightingale said: My love for the rose keeps me here. The hoopoe said: The rose blooms for a season and is gone; the Rose you seek blooms forever, and does not fade, and its garden is not a garden of this world. And the nightingale was silent, and his silence was the beginning of his flight.

The peacock said: My beauty was given me in paradise; if I leave this place I may lose it. The hoopoe said: What you call your beauty is a borrowed coat of paint; the Beauty you are painted after does not fade, and He is not jealous of His own reflection — He is pleased to see it in motion, flying home.
2: [Conference of the Birds — The seven valleys]

The road passes through seven valleys: the valley of the quest, of love, of knowledge, of detachment, of unity, of bewilderment, and of poverty and annihilation. At each valley, many of the birds turned back, and those who went on were fewer and lighter, until at the last valley they were thirty birds, and their feathers had been burned away by the wind of the journey, and they were glad.
[Conference of the Birds — The drop and the sea]

A drop said to the sea: I am afraid of you, for if I join you I will be lost. The sea said: If you join me you will be me, and I will be you, and nothing will be lost but the fear. And the drop understood, and fell, and the fall was not a fall but a homecoming, and the sea welcomed it as the shore welcomes the river.
[Conference of the Birds — The king's mirror]

A king hung a mirror in the market and said: Let him who sees his true face in it take the kingdom. Many looked and saw their clothes, their wealth, their anger; and they went away. One looked and saw the mirror itself, and the looking, and the king behind the mirror — and he was given the kingdom, for he had found the king, and the king is found only by those who stop looking at themselves.
3: At last the thirty birds came to the mountain, and they knocked at the gate, and the gate opened, and within was a light without a lamp, and a throne without a king, and they looked, and they saw the Simurgh — and the Simurgh is thirty birds, and the thirty birds are the Simurgh. Si murgh, in the old tongue: thirty birds. And they understood the name, and the name was the journey, and the journey was the king.
[Conference of the Birds — The last counsel]

And the voice said: You came seeking a king, and you found a mirror. Go back to the world, for the world is the mirror's other side, and every face in it is the king's, and every thirst is the sea calling to its drop. He who seeks the king in the palace will find a servant; he who seeks him in the thirsty will find the king.
[Conference of the Birds — The hoopoe's blessing]

And the hoopoe, who had led them, bowed to them at the end, for a guide's last duty is to kneel to those he guided. And the birds flew back to the world, and they were the same birds and not the same, and wherever they settled, the place became a little brighter, as if a window had been opened in a house that had forgotten it had windows.
